## The Location Landscape

Workplace flexibility is a significant factor for many candidates when choosing a job. Your policy position affects your ability to attract and retain people. We quote no candidate-preference survey figures here, because we have not cited a source for any. Ask your own candidates and employees.

### The Candidate View

Candidate preferences vary by role, life stage and market. For some, flexibility is close to non-negotiable. Track what candidates in your pipeline say, and which offers you lose over location policy.

### Policy Options

Models in practice:

- Full remote, any location
- Remote-first, with the office optional
- Hybrid, with some days in the office
- Office-first, with occasional remote work
- Full office, with required presence

### Compensation Implications

Location-based adjustments:

- Geographic pay differentials
- Remote work stipends
- Relocation packages
- Office commute benefits

### Hiring Strategy Alignment

Match policy to needs:

- Remote expands your talent pool
- On-site requirements limit geography
- Hybrid requires local candidates
- Clear communication prevents surprises

### Role-Specific Considerations

It is not one-size-fits-all:

- Some roles require presence
- Others are fully remote-capable
- Team dynamics matter
- Client expectations factor in

### Honest Positioning

Attract the right candidates:

- State the policy clearly in postings
- Discuss expectations early
- Be specific about flexibility
- Avoid bait-and-switch

### Future-Proofing

Plan for change:

- Policy may change
- Employee preferences shift
- Competitive pressures mount
- Technology enables new models

### Working With Your Policy

When you brief a role with TaaSFlow, state your workplace policy and where candidates can be based, so the shortlist reflects it. TaaSFlow is a recruiting platform with managed execution. Agents source and score candidates, a recruiter reviews every shortlist before you see it, and you make every hiring decision.

Your location policy is a talent strategy decision, not just an operations choice.
